introduction_markdown: Answer BOTH sections in the SAME answer booklet, beginning each section on a new page. You are advised to begin with SECTION A. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. Read all instructions on BOTH the question paper and the answer booklet very carefully. Failure to obey these instructions or to number your work as on the question paper will cause you to lose marks. Any unusual mark, sign or unnecessary disclosure of your identity will be considered as an attempt to cheat and will earn you a penalty. In the Directed Writing question avoid indiscriminate copying of portions of the passage as your answer because this will earn you no marks. A pre-prepared or memorised composition will earn you no marks. Duration: two hours.

questions.enonce_markdown:
**SECTION A - DIRECTED WRITING (30 marks)**

Mark distribution: Content (14 marks); Expression and Accuracy (12 marks); Slanting (4 marks).

**You are Azoh Cynthia, Secretary of Mbat Development Association (MADA). On the 31st of October 2021, at 4pm, your association held an end-of-month meeting to raise funds to carry out some developmental projects in the village. Selecting relevant materials from the discussion below, develop the minutes of the meeting focusing on the resolutions arrived at concerning the raising of funds and the projects to be funded. Write in two paragraphs of not more than 150 words, paying attention to format, grammar, spelling, punctuation and handwriting.**

**Chairperson:** I wish to welcome you all to this very important meeting which is intended to lay the ground works for fund raising towards the realization of some developmental projects in our village. Before we delve into the business of the day, I will like to find out from the secretary if everyone invited is present.

**Secretary:** Thank you Mr President. Apart from Mr Teddy and Mrs Mbonteh, every other person is present.

**Chairperson:** In spite of their absence, we will begin our meeting. Can the secretary read out the agenda of the meeting?.

**Secretary:** (Reads out the agenda.)

**Chairperson:** Thank you Mrs Azoh. Has any item been left out.

**Abang:** I think the agenda is correct.

**Epumah:** Mr Chairperson before we get there, I wish to find out if the marital problem between Mr and Mrs Kang has been resolved?

**Chairperson:** Yes. I must add that Mr Kang was very apologetic. He explained that he was drunk at the time of the incident. He has since paid his fine and has stopped drinking. Let's move on to the main business of the day - fund raising. Organizing Secretary, over to you.

**Secretary:** Thank you Mr Chairperson. The floor is now open to proposals and suggestions.

**Bouba:** I feel that our monthly contributions should be increased from 1,000 FCFA to 3,000 FCFA, given the importance of the projects.

**Epunah:** For me, we should consider buying enough drinks for the occasion.

**Bouba:** I don't buy Epunah's idea. I rather think we should send out appeal letters to Guinness Cameroon SA, the American Embassy and GTZ. Fund raising could also be added to our end-of-year get-together. We could send invitation letters to our friends to come and support us. During the occasion, there could be activities like cutting of the cake and popping of champagne, all geared towards raising money. In the evening of that day, we could have a gala night open to the public upon the payment of gate money.

**Chairperson:** Thank you Bouba. Has anyone got something to add or subtract from the suggestions?

**Ekih-Muh:** I support the idea of raising the monthly contributions to 3,000 FCFA.

**Chairperson:** Ok. But don't forget that we have projects other than water to fund. Our village market needs to be renovated. We also need to renovate our primary school as well as provide prizes regularly at all prize award ceremonies.

**Chongong:** Chairman, we can also raise funds by buying a cow at Christmas and slaughtering it for members to buy. The profit will then be used for our projects.

**Members:** (Clapping happily) Good, very good!

**Chairperson:** I take your reaction as a sign of approval.

**Members:** Yes! Yes!

**Epumah:** Before we conclude, ladies and gentlemen remember we have an outstanding debt since last year; it will be a good idea if we take care of it.

**Neba:** Less I forget, some funds could be kept aside to motivate our hardworking executive members.

**Chairperson:** Thank you for your contributions. We look forward to implementing the resolutions arrived at during this meeting.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Model answer (minutes with a heading and a signature; the two paragraphs of the body have 143 words)**

**MINUTES OF THE END-OF-MONTH MEETING OF MBAT DEVELOPMENT ASSOCIATION (MADA) HELD ON 31ST OCTOBER 2021 AT 4 PM**

The meeting resolved to raise funds in several ways. Members agreed that the monthly contribution be increased from 1,000 FCFA to 3,000 FCFA. Appeal letters will be sent to Guinness Cameroon SA, the American Embassy and GTZ, and invitation letters will be sent to friends of the association. Fund raising will also be added to the end-of-year get-together, with the cutting of a cake, the popping of champagne and a gala night open to the public on payment of gate money. Finally, a cow will be bought at Christmas, slaughtered and sold to members.

The money raised will finance the renovation of the village market and of the primary school, and regular prizes for school award ceremonies. Members also resolved to pay the outstanding debt of last year and to set some funds aside to motivate the hardworking executive members.

Azoh Cynthia, Secretary

**Why this works (selection and slanting).** The task is to write the MINUTES, so the heading gives the name of the association, the date and the time, and the signature gives the Secretary's name (Azoh Cynthia) and her title. The body keeps only what the task asks for, in two paragraphs. Paragraph 1 gives the RESOLUTIONS on raising funds: the contribution raised from 1,000 FCFA to 3,000 FCFA, the appeal letters to Guinness Cameroon SA, the American Embassy and GTZ, the invitations to friends, the end-of-year get-together (cake, champagne, gala night with gate money) and the cow bought at Christmas and sold to members. Paragraph 2 gives the PROJECTS to be funded (the village market, the primary school, prizes at award ceremonies) and the two other money decisions (the outstanding debt, funds kept aside to motivate the executive). The model leaves out everything that is not about funds or projects: the welcome, the absence of Mr Teddy and Mrs Mbonteh, the agenda, and the marital problem of Mr and Mrs Kang. It also leaves out Epunah's idea of buying drinks, which Bouba rejected. The decisions are reported in the passive and in the future ("will be sent"), as minutes do, in the candidate's own words.

**Marking guide**

| Criterion | Marks | What earns the marks |
|---|---|---|
| Content | 14 | The resolutions on fund raising (higher contributions, appeal and invitation letters, end-of-year event with gala night, cow at Christmas) AND the projects to be funded (market, primary school, prizes); the outstanding debt and the funds for the executive are accepted as extra points; no irrelevant points |
| Expression and Accuracy | 12 | Own words (no lifting of whole sentences or of the dialogue), reported (not direct) speech, linking, correct grammar, spelling and punctuation, TWO paragraphs, 150 words at most |
| Slanting | 4 | Every point is turned into a decision or resolution (not a chat); the personal matter (Mr Kang), the absentees and the rejected proposal are left out; correct format of minutes (heading with name, date and time; signed by the Secretary) |

**Common mistakes**

1. Copying the speeches of the dialogue word for word, or keeping the speakers' names and direct speech instead of writing the decisions taken.
2. Including irrelevant matter (the absentees, the agenda, the marital problem of Mr and Mrs Kang) or forgetting the projects to be funded.
3. Writing a letter or a report instead of minutes (no heading, no signature), using one paragraph or three, or going over 150 words.

Le scan laisse apparaitre en filigrane le texte du verso (transparence) ; il a ete ignore. Le corps du modele compte 143 mots ; titre et signature compris, 161 mots (la limite de 150 mots s'applique au texte des deux paragraphes).
